stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: A fly sits on the roof of car A moving at speed $v_A$. Pick a reference frame (road, pedestrian, car B) and press TRACE to draw the fly's trajectory. Change frames and change $v_A$ to see how the same motion produces different trajectories.
stages.concept: A **trajectory** is the set of successive positions of a point, and it always depends on the chosen **reference frame** (référentiel). The fly's ground-frame motion is $x(t) = x_0 + v_A\,t$ with a small vertical hop. Change the observer, and the shape of the trajectory changes.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Three ghosted target trajectories are shown. For each one, pick the reference frame and set $v_A$ so your TRACE matches the ghost. A live preview shows the shape you're about to draw.
stages.concept: In the car-A frame, the fly only bobs vertically. In the road frame, its path stretches to the right at $v_A$. In a frame moving at $v_F$, the horizontal velocity of the fly becomes $v_A - v_F$ — negative velocity flips the trajectory to the left.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The live preview is hidden. Read each ghosted target trajectory and reason on paper about which reference frame produced it and what value of $v_A$ is needed. You have limited traces — no spray-and-pray.
stages.concept: Ask yourself: which observer sees the fly move to the right? to the left? not at all? For horizontal travel over $T = 3\,\text{s}$, the trace length in metres equals $|v_A - v_F| \cdot T$. A vertical-only ghost means $v_A - v_F = 0$.

labels.tip1: pick a frame, move v_A, then TRACE
labels.tip2: use the dashed preview to line up each ghost
labels.tip3: compute v_A − v_frame from the ghost, then TRACE
labels.peek_tip_relative: In a frame moving at v_F, the fly's horizontal velocity is v_A − v_F. A leftward trace means v_F > v_A.
labels.peek_tip_dot: A vertical-only trace (no horizontal drift) means v_A − v_frame = 0. Match the frame's velocity to v_A.
labels.peek_tip_length: Trace duration is 3 s. Horizontal length in metres ≈ |v_A − v_frame| · 3.

1.1: Pick a frame from the panel on the left, then press TRACE.
1.2: Try the same v_A in two different frames — the trajectory shape changes.
1.3: In the car-A frame the fly barely moves horizontally: the car and the fly share the same velocity.

2.1: The dashed preview shows the trace you're about to draw. Adjust v_A and swap frames until it overlaps the ghost.
2.2: A horizontal ghost heading right means v_A > v_frame. Heading left means v_A < v_frame.
2.3: A vertical-only ghost means v_A − v_frame = 0: the fly appears stationary along x.

3.1: There's no preview. Read each ghost and figure out which observer sees it before touching the controls.
3.2: Trace length ≈ |v_A − v_frame| · 3 s. Direction tells you the sign of v_A − v_frame.
3.3: If the ghost is a vertical hop, pick the frame whose velocity matches v_A. If it drifts left, pick a frame moving faster than v_A.
